History of recurrent otitis externa in the past year supports an underlying atopic or allergic dermatitis process. No systemic signs reported. Leading concern is canine atopic dermatitis, with flea allergy dermatitis and secondary Malassezia/bacterial pyoderma as contributing or complicating factors.

pp-1004.clinicalSummary: 9-year-old male neutered Boxer with a 3-week history of a right lateral thoracic skin/subcutaneous mass that has grown from pea- to grape-sized, with intermittent erythema and swelling ('waxing and waning'). This fluctuating redness and rapid growth pattern is consistent with mast cell degranulation (Darier's sign), and Boxers are a breed with well-documented predisposition to mast cell tumors. Prior history of benign lipoma excision is reassuring but not directly relevant given the different clinical behavior described here. Physical exam, fine needle aspiration cytology, and regional lymph node palpation are needed to characterize the mass before any surgical planning.

pp-1007.clinicalSummary: 5-year-old male castrated Maine Coon presenting with a 12-hour history of stranguria, pollakiuria, vocalization in the litter box, vomiting, lethargy, and hiding, with a prior episode of hematuria last year. This presentation is classic for feline lower urinary tract disease with likely urethral obstruction, especially given the anuria and systemic signs (vomiting, lethargy) suggesting possible post-renal azotemia and hyperkalemia. Physical exam should prioritize bladder palpation (large, firm, painful bladder supports obstruction), perineal/penile exam for urethral plug or stricture, and assessment for bradycardia or other signs of hyperkalemia. This is a time-sensitive emergency until obstruction is ruled out.
